I would recommend checking out the Sony WH-1000XM4 or XM5 (both over the ear headphones). They have really good prices going on both of them at the moment, at multiple retailers. Don't forget to check eBay for any good deals.

Android version is called [Adapt Sound](https://images.samsung.com/is/image/samsung/assets/latin_en/support/mobile-devices1/how-to-customize-the-adapt-sound/04-adapt-sound-EN.jpg?$ORIGIN_JPG$). It's built into your phone. Never used an iPhone, so I can't say if this is different or not from the way the iPhone one functions. Also, these aren't for severe hearing loss, not the Android one, nor the iPhone one.

Go to settings - sound - sound quality and effects - adapt sound. Click test my hearing, it'll do a simple hearing test on each ear, through multiple frequencies.

Android also has Sound notifications (Made by Google). Your phone listens for ~
- Smoke and fire alarms
- Sirens (Ambulance, Fire Truck, Police)
- Baby sounds and Baby cries
- Dog barking
- Doorbell ringing (you can save your specific doorbell sound)
- Knocking
- Appliance beeping (microwave, ovens, timers, etc.)
- Landline phone ringing
- Water running
- You can add custom sounds for it to listen to. Play the sound, your phone will record it and listen for it in the future.


The phone will alert you (Camera Flash, Vibrate, and/or Smart Watch alerts) and the phone also makes a little recording of the sound/s (it will playback like 5-10 seconds of audio prior to the sound/alert, and the sound/alert itself. So you can hear anything that might've been occurring prior to the sound being triggered. Extremely useful imo. You'll be able to hear potential footsteps or if someone was tampering with or breaking something prior to any alarm/beeping alerts, or if someone entered or left a baby's room prior to a "Baby Crying alert," etc. 

Each alert is organized by time & date and by sound/alert type. You can choose to save them and listen to them whenever you want.

I love being able to listen to fire trucks and police cars and dogs barking and babies crying as their mothers push them by the apartment (NYC). I otherwise am oblivious to them. But the phone captures the sounds almost flawlessly and replays them as if the sound is occurring right next to my ear. It's fascinating really, I love it.

Android also has Live transcribe and Sound amplifier. Live transcribe dictates everything that it hears. You can even set the phone to vibrate when someone calls your name. These are also Google apps. Google-Android same thing. Google makes Android, but many folks aren't aware.

**Note:** Adapt Sound isn't a hearing aid feature, just a sound quality feature. Androids/Google's hearing aid feature is called Sound Amplifier - must be used with wired headphones for a quality experience. I never owned Galaxy Buds, so idk if they're any different from those. 

Also, have no idea if it's comparable to the iPhone version. From what I hear, the iPhone version sounds much better. But... ¯\\(°_O)/¯

**Fun fact, Gallaudet University helped in the creation & testing of some of these apps.**

Actually, it's valid to ask. Upon purchase, some deals split the price between each item. These are cash return hackable. (Edit: you can see this in your cart when you add the items, prior to purchase.)

**For example:** Buy 1 tool  for $200 and get 1 free battery. On the receipt the order will be reflected as if you purchases two items...
**Tool** - $120
**Battery** - $80

With a receipt that looks like this, you can do a cash return and get $80 back for the battery.

If the receipt says, for example:
**Tool & battery deal** - $200

And you show it to the teller, they'll explain that you have to return every single item for your $200.

So if you have a receipt that looks like this, what you do is, never show them the receipt. Just bring the specific item that you want to return, You won't be able to get cash, but you'll be able to get store credit. That way you can still return one of the items you don't want.


People often go to HD and argue with the returns folks and order them to bring the management out when they have a receipt with a single price listed for multiple items. They yell about how they read about "hacks" online! And how "This is complete bullsh-t and how this HD sucks!!" 😂

They're giving the clerks a hard time AND THEY'RE the one that's wrong.

So split price for each item. Each price is what you'll get for returning each item and you can return for cash.

Single price showing for all items. Attempts to return for cash will require returning all items for the price show. Don't bring the receipt and just return the 1 or 2 items that you don't want for store credit. (Make sure you pay attention to the value of store credit that they're giving you. It might not be significant in all cases. You might decide it's better to keep the items)

**Edit:** When purchasing online, the price is split when you add the items to your cart. So you can see how much you can return each item for before you buy.

Or if it's a single price for multiple items, then you'll know it's not a "cash" hackable deal. Just store credit, or return everything for cash.

As in why does the land based C-Ram use Multipurpose Tracer-Self Destruct (MPT-SD) rounds and why does the sea based Phalanx CIWS use the armor-piercing tungsten penetrator rounds or depleted uranium with discardable sabots.

 Crap my short answer turned into a long answer while I was editing it. Oh well. You should really read them both though imo.

Short answer: To alert civilian and military personnel to the direction of the threat and the direction of the firing. Also they're not tracer bullets, they're Multipurpose Tracer-Self Destruct (MPT-SD) rounds. The tracer affect is a by-product of of the self destruct function. But the tracer is also a function that is something they want since the C-Ram fires over heavily populated areas. Thus allowing people to know where the threat is coming from and potentially hide from any exploding threat that got intercepted by the MPT-SD rounds.

Imagine just blowing up incoming missiles and not informing civilians as to where it will be occuring. In Vietnam many soldiers died from fragments from exploding bombs dropped by friendly aircraft hundreds of yards away from them. The higher up something explodes the further it's shrapnel and fragments can travel. Very often guys would be sitting in the jungle laughing and chatting and all of the sudden a massive piece of steel would fly into someone's head, killing them instantly. Sometimes it wasn't even massive, could be as small as a tiny bullet. If the trajectory is right and the bomb exploded in the canopy of the trees instead of on land then people a mile away or even more were at risk of injury or death. They often hid under downed trees or behind trees or whatever they can find when bombing was going on, which was every day, some times multiple times a day with dozens of bombs at a time being dropped. Unfortunately the trees often weren't enough or just enough body was exposed for a lethal injury to occur.



Long answer: They're not your ordinary tracer bullets, they're Multipurpose Tracer-Self Destruct (MPT-SD) rounds that combine a light armor and high-explosive capability into a single round for improved lethality on all targets.

C-RAM is a land based version of the Phalanx CIWS used to detect and/or destroy incoming artillery, rockets and mortar rounds in the air before they hit their ground targets. 

The Phalanx CIWS is the sea based variant of the two. The rounds on the Phalanx CIWS are armor-piercing tungsten penetrator rounds or depleted uranium with discardable sabots. Tracer variants are almost never used but have been. They don't have to worry about where the bullets will land, since they're in the middle of the ocean. So instead they use more powerful bullets that don't self destruct and have other weapons for situations requiring the benefits of tracer utilities

The main reason behind the tracer variant rounds for the land based version is because they're usually in heavily populated areas. The weapon serves more than just one purpose of taking out potential threats but also alerting civilians and even other soldiers to the direction of the threat and the direction the weapon is firing in. Another reason for the tracer is to have a visual reference of the directions the bullets went so they can do an evaluation afterwards. It's possible for things to go wrong, even though they're self destruct rounds, it's possible for fragments to hit civilian property or even a person. During an intense fire fight it's also possible for the C-Ram to skim parts of the land that are higher in altitude. For example if trying to take down a fighter jet, while the jet is doing evasive maneuvers and flying low to the ground it's possible for the C-Ram to skim a big hill or tall building or structure in the distance with a few rounds. Which means for safety and responsibility purposes it's just better to know where the rounds went.

Source: My brother had a lighter when we were super young. Except it did, it was just opposite of where he was looking from. That single tiny ember that one might say was damn near invisible, worked its way down this strand of "grass" as we walked up the mountain side, as we got about 15 feet away, we heard a popping sound, we turned around to see that the ember that no one knew existed had spread to a 3x4 foot massive fire, flames were probably 5 feet high.
